description: WORKED EXAMPLE, rebuilt 2026-10-02 on a MEASURED boundary: a 3-option `choice` on this head answers MEDIUM for both a 13-word and a 412-word document (measured: labels frozen across a 77x range, band=low every time), so the classification is built from TWO threshold questions chained. Each threshold question is TWO decide nodes, because one route matches exactly one payload field: the GATE routes on `band` (R3 -- a low-confidence answer escalates, it never nominates a branch) and the ASK routes on `label` (the yes/no branch) and is only reachable through the gate. The gate and the ask send the identical state+question, so the ask's answer is the answer the gate just cleared; both calls' bands are visible in the run report. TWO MEASURED ENGINE FACTS shape this file. (1) There is NO shell->route interpolation: `decide.prompt` is forwarded verbatim (crates/laya-graph/src/lower.rs:104) and a route's upstream must be an mcp node (crates/laya-graph/src/route_exec.rs:68-76), so the word count is a LITERAL in the prompt; the `wc -w` shell node prints the true count into the run report so a reader can check the literal against it. (2) A flow decide is ALWAYS a choice on the wire: LiveMcpCaller rebuilds it as {type: choice, criteria: {option: option}} (crates/laya-cli/src/mcp_client.rs:106-120), so the questions here are 2-option choices over yes/no -- `noul` (options empty) would be a choice with empty criteria, which laya-mcp refuses (crates/laya-mcp/src/lib.rs:418-428). Measured on this shape: 13 -> no, 412 -> yes, all three executed gates band mid; the phrasing 'The word count in the file is N words.' + 'Is the word count greater than T words?' was chosen over 5 candidates measured in _docs/02-guides/wc-example/. Its pairing control is wc-classify-chained.control.flow.json: the identical shape over a 412-word document, which must reach a DIFFERENT terminal branch.
